title: Aftershift incident actions and follow-ups
body:
Quick aftershift notes from the 02:14 UTC paging spike (v1 generate 503s). Raw brain-dump so I don't forget anything — will tidy and hand over at next cadence.

Summary:
- Time window: 02:12–02:47 UTC (saw intermittent 503s start ~02:12).
- Impact: ~6% of requests to /v1/generate returned 503s during peak of the window. Latency for healthy requests spiked from p50=80ms to p95=4200ms.
- Likely root cause (first-pass): sudden descheduling of a small subset of inference workers while autoscaler lagged; combined with cache-priming storm that caused some pods to OOM-kill during KV-cache warmup.

Immediate actions taken (on-call):
- 02:15: scaled inference pool from 24->36 for region-us-west to absorb traffic (manual override).
- 02:18: drained pod inference-idx-7 (OOM loops) and set node-affinity to avoid older kernel nodes.
- 02:25: rolled a tiny configuration tweak: lowered per-request max-seq to 1024 for model-x-4k to limit memory blowouts for cold KV cache.
- 02:30: turned on circuit-breaker route to fallback-model (lighter quantized variant) for 30m to reduce token cost/pressure.

What I observed in logs/metrics (notes to self):
- k8s events: repeated OOMKilled for inference-idx-6/7; container logs show growth in kv-cache allocation during first 3 requests after restart.
- Node kubelet had recent 5.10 kernel; suspiciously the older nodes show slightly higher page fault counters. Compare with nodes added during last infra rollout.
- Autoscaler (custom HPA) didn't kick immediately — metrics ingestion laged ~38s which delayed scale-up. Need to quantify threshold.

Runbook gaps / TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Update runbook section "KV cache warmup" with explicit mitigation steps: shock scale-up, temp fallback-model, and pod cordon sequence. Assign: Priya. Due: 2026-04-02.
- [ ] Add an automated post-start health-check that runs small warmup requests to prefill KV cache; if failed, mark pod NotReady until warmup completes. Assign: Rafael. Due: 2026-04-09.
- [ ] Investigate autoscaler telemetry ingestion delay — add alert if metric latency >20s. Assign: me (Izzy). Due: 2026-03-30.
- [ ] Create a targeted test that simulates tens of cold-start requests to validate memory behavior (loadtest in sandbox). Assign: eng-serving-runtime. Linked ticket: INF-4721.
- [ ] Add node filter rule to avoid scheduling inference pods on kernel-older-than:5.12 nodes until tested. Ops/Infra to sync.

Follow-ups for postmortem draft:
- Timeline: capture exact minutes for each step from pager -> mitigation -> stabilization. I have timeline markers in Slack thread (see linked).
- Impact quant: correlate 503s to customer tokens and estimate billing exposure. Ask finance for quick estimate if needed.
- Root-cause hypothesis to vet: node-level memory fragmentation + cache warmup pattern -> OOM kill -> autoscaler lag. We need to reproduce.

Quick commands / pointers I used (save for runbook):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep inference-idx
- kubectl logs -n inference inference-idx-7 --since=10m --tail=500
- curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"model-x-4k","input":"warmup"}'
- k get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 100

Questions / open unknowns:
- Why were only a subset of pods affected? (Affinity? Node kernel differences?)
- Is the autoscaler metric aggregator single point that could lag under load?
- Any recent infra rollout that touched node images in us-west? Check infra change log for last 72h.

Hand-off notes for next on-call (Priya or Rafael):
- Focus areas: autoscaler metric latency, add warmup probe, reproduce with sandbox loadtest.
- If similar spike returns: enact temporary fallback-model (script saved at /ops/fallback-scripts/fallback-light.sh) and open INF-incident channel.
- Do not revert scale-down for at least 20m after stabilization; observe p95 and 503 rate.

Misc (random):
- Quick wins: add a simple per-pod prefork warmup hook (run 3 short requests) in startup script — low effort, likely high value.
- We should measure cold-start memory curve for each model variant and publish profiles in Optimize console.

Notes-to-self: draft postmortem skeleton tomorrow morning; double-check OOM logs and node kernel versions.

End of notes. Will convert into tidy incident doc + runbook changes.

Izzy
